title: Startup = Growth: why growth rate is the compass for every startup decision
summary: Paul Graham argues a startup is a company designed to grow fast, and everything else (funding, acquisitions, technology) follows from growth. Founders should know their weekly growth rate, pick a target, and use it to make every decision, letting growth pressure evolve the idea.

principles.text: A startup is defined by growth, not by tech, funding or an exit; everything else follows from it.
principles.quote: A startup is a company designed to grow fast. Being newly founded does not in itself make a company a startup.

principles.text: Know your growth rate as a ratio, not an absolute count of new customers.
principles.quote: What matters is not the absolute number of new customers, but the ratio of new customers to existing ones.

principles.text: Benchmark weekly growth: 5-7% is good, 10% exceptional, 1% means you haven't figured it out yet.
principles.quote: A good growth rate during YC is 5-7% a week. If you can hit 10% a week you're doing exceptionally well.

principles.text: Pick a target growth rate and just hit it every week; use it to decide everything.
principles.quote: You can use that target growth rate to make all your decisions for you; anything that gets you the growth you need is ipso facto right.

principles.text: Use growth as evolutionary pressure: modify the idea until it grows, and follow it past your initial vision.
principles.quote: anything that grows consistently at 10% a week is almost certainly a better idea than you started with.

principles.text: Act rather than over-strategize; weekly targets force action, which is the high bit of success.
principles.quote: Nine times out of ten, sitting around strategizing is just a form of procrastination.
